guidelines.detail: same as LRN-008 (The description places identifying the need before issuing the proposal request. The generated model represented that action as a start event instead of the distinct task expected in the reference, leaving the task and its flow absent. This is essentially the situation covered by LRN-008.)

same as LRN-007 (The label pairs and description show that labels should preserve the meaning and distinctions of the described activities and outcome. LRN-007 already expresses this guidance; the proposed wording is a generalized equivalent.)

same as LRN-009 (The description presents information-gathering as optional before the required analysis and selection. The records show the optional activity and the branch-and-merge structure are absent from the generated model; no extra_element records were provided. LRN-009 already states this guideline essentially the same way.)

refines FID-02 (The description names site visits and interviews as distinct alternatives, while the records show the generated model combined them and the reference modeled an interview separately. This adds a specific application of FID-02 for alternative activities without assuming whether the alternatives are mutually exclusive.)

refines GW-02 (The description makes the site visits or interviews optional, and the records show the reference has a task and gateways for the optional path and its merge that are not represented correspondingly in the generated model. This guideline specifies how to model an optional activity; it refines the documented exclusive-split guidance. No extra_element records were provided to indicate an alternative )

same as LRN-007 (The description states meaningful start and end conditions, while the reference labels those events generically (P1, P2, S1, S7). LRN-007 already expresses the same general labeling principle; FID-03 also supports faithful labels.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a participant performs an action that initiates the process: Model the process trigger with a start event, then model the participant’s described action as a distinct task; do not use the action itself as the start event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant identifies or recognizes a need as an action that initiates the process, before describing subsequent work

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description distinguishes a process trigger, an activity, or an outcome from other stages of the process: Label each BPMN element according to the meaning of its corresponding described trigger, activity, or outcome; do not substitute a different stage or its purpose or result.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description distinguishes activities or states a process outcome

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an activity may or may not occur before a later required activity: model the optional activity as one branch of an exclusive gateway, and merge the branches before the later required activity
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an activity may occur before a later required activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents two or more distinct activities as alternatives: Model each activity as a separate task on its own branch rather than combining the alternatives into one task; choose a gateway that matches whether one or multiple alternatives may be performed.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents two or more distinct activities as alternatives

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says an additional activity may be performed before a later activity that follows regardless: Model the additional activity as a distinct optional path that rejoins the main flow before the later shared activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says an additional activity may be performed before a later activity that follows regardless
